premises.text: Most men hate clothes shopping online because they distrust fit and do not know where to start
premises.evidence_span: when it comes to shopping online, he has no idea where to even start. When it comes to fit, Joe just doesn't trust e-commerce

premises.text: Branded is a marketplace connecting men who hate shopping with personal shoppers who love to shop
premises.evidence_span: marketplace that connects men who hate shopping with people that love to shop

premises.text: MAIL collects style, size, and preference data to match men to shoppers and improve recommendations
premises.evidence_span: Mail collects a bunch of data about what Joe likes to wear and what he doesn't, his sizes and his style

premises.text: Shoppers find items from any e-commerce site or boutique and add them to the cart in a real-time conversation
premises.evidence_span: They find stuff from any e-commerce site in the world

premises.text: Try-on with pickup returns (return like a man) solves fit without post-office friction; charge kept items plus shopper tip
premises.evidence_span: giving him the best return service in the industry. We call it return like a man

premises.text: Supply of style-capable underemployed shoppers can be recruited and trained at scale
premises.evidence_span: finding people that would love to make money by shopping for our men isn't a hard sell

value.text: Average men get trusted human help shopping for clothes online with try-before-you-buy fit
value.evidence_span: connects men who hate shopping with people that love to shop. And we let you try stuff on before you buy it

causal_links.evidence_span: unlike in a store, this person's got all this data about what he likes and what he doesn't
93% of men still shop for clothes offline
shopping for clothes isn't an exact science. It's personal. It requires a human touch
shopping for fit is probably one of the biggest reasons why men don't shop online
plenty of time to make money by shopping for our men

notes: Where-to-start and fit distrust folded as one men's e-commerce pain-bundle in P1. Waitlist traction and team credentials excluded. Tip-on-kept-items kept as commercial detail of P5. Singletons D1, D3, D4 retained as separately revisable demand, returns, and labor-supply modules.
